column1: # OCTOPATH TRAVELER 0 (Chinese release): Square Enix, Unreal Engine 5 (the paged global distance field shaders and the LowLevelTasks task system; mobile renderer, SF_GLSL_SWITCH_MOBILE shaders), SDK 19.0.0 (the update's 21.2.0), NVN, CRIWARE sound and movies; update 1.0.5.
# The Asian release of the same game (Chinese and Korean; its NACP's first title is the Korean one, the Chinese one is 歧路旅人0): the same engine and the same assets as the international release
# (01005270232F2000), but its own main build, whose engine data sits 0x3000 bytes higher (the allocator's object and vtable, the console variables).
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and brought up on the phone (docs/agents)
# The version number is the update NCA's own (the number a dump's [v<N>] tag names), not the display version the NACP holds: the Asian release numbers its updates as the
# international one does (its 1.0.2 is v131072 and its 1.0.4 v262144, the international one's as well), so its 1.0.5 is v327680; this build is that update's (main e3e401c2…, the
# 1.0.5 update build of the patch title 01001300232F4800)
# subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie (main imports from it)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game's config caps Unreal at 30 (t.MaxFPS 30, FrameRateLimit 30, and rhi.SyncInterval 2, the present interval 2 it asks for); the host writes t.MaxFPS 60 and
# rhi.SyncInterval 1 into its console variables (hle_fpslock.c), so the game asks for present interval 1 itself. Unreal steps the game by the time that really passed.
# DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) keeps the game's 30 and saves power
# Unreal Engine: nninitStartup (main+0x12a50) needs virtual address memory and reserves one address region for the engine (-SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize= in MB, game_args below; 62 GB by default).

# Its allocator, an FMallocBinned3 (37 GB of address space), is replaced by the host's (patches.py cut, hle_uemalloc.c), and the SDK's node area is cut to 62 MB (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py), so the region holds what the engine maps
# itself (709 MB at character creation, spread over 1 GB). Alias region = node area + up to 1 GB of alignment (regions of 1 GB and more are 1 GB aligned) + the 2 GB region; 256 MB stacks, 128 MB heap
# the NPDM declares 80 MB of system resource, so the SDK answers that virtual address memory is enabled (the host's 32 MB default would do as well)

# 61 vertex shaders pick one of several c2 table slots at run time (separate texture slots 0-10, samplers 0-4), which the translator cannot trace to one slot: slot indices in c2, the bound slots in its arrays
# The decoded shader code archives: the engine's global shaders and the game's material shaders

column1: # The shaders are in the shader code archives of the pak (ShaderArchive-*.ushaderbytecode), each one Oodle-compressed; the NSP script decodes them on the Mac with the game's own Oodle (uepak.py, DM_OODLE_JOB),
